Notes: A seabird catches fish from the water's surface; it also steals fish from other birds; it does not dive underwater in either case; the goal is to emphasize a similarity.
33.1.stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

opts.A: The bird feeds mainly on small sea animals.
opts.B: Only one method involves stealing from other birds.
opts.C: Neither method requires the bird to dive underwater.
opts.D: The bird can catch fish in more than one way.

33.2.body: In a university archive, scholars examined correspondence, field notes, and early drafts that revealed how a project changed over time. The materials did not overturn the basic history of the project, but they clarified the roles of several participants and made one previously simple interpretation seem less adequate. Notes: A desert fox eats insects it digs from sand; it also eats fruit that has fallen from shrubs; both methods require foraging at night; the goal is to emphasize a similarity.
33.2.stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

opts.A: Both ways the desert fox gets food involve nighttime foraging.
opts.B: The fox digs insects from sand.
opts.D: The fox eats insects and fruit.

33.3.body: A museum catalog presents an artist, object, or performance in relation to the social and technical conditions that shaped it. Instead of merely naming the work, the catalog connects materials, audience, historical moment, and purpose so readers can understand why a particular description or conclusion is warranted. Notes: A heron catches fish in shallow water; it also catches frogs near reeds; both methods involve standing still before striking quickly; the goal is to emphasize a similarity.
33.3.stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

opts.C: Both feeding methods involve standing still before a quick strike.

33.4.body: The study notes that the same policy may produce different results when transportation, housing, funding, and public trust vary from place to place. A public-policy study compares outcomes across several communities that adopted similar measures under different local conditions. Because the evidence includes exceptions as well as broad patterns, the researchers choose cautious wording and distinguish between what the data directly show and what they merely suggest. Notes: A monkey cracks nuts with stones; it also opens shellfish with stones; both methods involve using tools to access protected food; the goal is to emphasize a similarity.
33.4.stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

opts.B: Both food-gathering methods involve using tools to open protected food.
opts.C: Stones can be used as tools.
opts.D: The monkey eats nuts and shellfish.

33.5.body: Additional trials were conducted under slightly changed conditions so the researchers could determine whether the initial pattern was stable or accidental. In a scientific investigation, the outcome depends on a sequence of observations rather than on one dramatic discovery. The researchers describe the method, the comparison group, and the limits of the evidence before drawing a conclusion that must be stated with both precision and restraint. Notes: A gull skims insects from a lake surface; it also snatches floating scraps near fishing boats; neither method requires diving; the goal is to emphasize a similarity.
33.5.stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

opts.A: The gull sometimes feeds near boats.
opts.D: Neither way of acquiring food requires the gull to dive below the surface.
